quotes.name: Coen Cartier
quotes.quote: After the scare, I stopped treating my body like it was somebody else's problem. This week that meant actually taking the doctor's advice and getting my blood pressure checked on my day off — cost me a morning I would've spent helping my daughter move some furniture. And I asked for a later shift start twice so I could walk the ten blocks instead of driving. It's not dramatic, but it's the kind of thing I used to put off. The money part is the co-pay, which is what it is. The time part is the part that stings — but I figure I owe it to my kids to stick around a little longer.

quotes.name: Yu Zen
quotes.quote: I've been in since C105 — that's the workplace accident. Twelve cycles now, give or take. The care's been steady, I'll say that. The nurses know my name, my wife's been here every visiting window, and the doctors have been straight with me about what recovery looks like. It's not fast. But I'm stable, and stable is a lot more than some folks get. You asked about the path out — from my side of the bed, it's about getting strong enough to walk out on my own two feet, then getting home to my kids. That's the whole plan. I know Chinatown's carrying the heaviest load in this city, and I know there are more sick people than there are beds with names attached. I'm one of the lucky ones — I've got a bed, I've got insurance, I've got family. Not everybody in this city can say that, and that gap keeps me up at night as much as the recovery does.

quotes.name: Maurice Franklin
quotes.quote: A severe flu can land you in the hospital when it stops being just a flu. I kept telling myself it was a bad cold, pushed through work, and by the time I couldn't catch my breath walking to the kitchen, my body had made the decision for me. The recovery timeline from the inside is slow and humbling. You don't bounce back; you crawl back. Days blur together, and every small step—sitting up, taking a few steps, eating a real meal—feels like a victory. And even after you're discharged, you're not done. You're still weak, still tired, still catching your breath. It took me a long while to feel like myself again, and I'm still careful. The hospital stay is just the beginning; the real recovery is the quiet, patient work of getting your strength back, day by day.

quotes.name: Deacon Seymour
quotes.quote: I spent my own stretch in a hospital bed not long ago, and I know what it's like to have your name on the door, to have people checking on you. But I also know that bed I was in—that was one bed, and there are a lot more filled by folks nobody's naming. Chinatown's carrying more sickness than anywhere else in this city, and if only a handful of those folks are getting named out loud, that's not a care trail, that's a gap. And gaps like that don't close by themselves.
